correctness.rationale: Integrating the top-hat difference on each Fourier mode gives the positive product symbol p_beta(t) with limits 1/3 and 2 beta. To justify the uniform ratio rather than ratios on unrelated grids, approximate each of an arbitrary pair of finite positive frequencies on the same grid of spacing h=2 pi delta/L, then let h tend to zero. Finite frequencies approach both limiting spectral endpoints. For beta>0 the symbol has positive infimum by compactness and the endpoint limits. The inequality p_beta≥1/3 at all frequencies is exactly beta≥sup H. Sine's upper Taylor bound and the negative sine on [pi,2 pi] give H≤1/6 through 2 pi, whereas H(5 pi/2)>1/6 and the limits of H are 1/20 and 1/6. The envelope t/[6(t−1)]−t^-2 bounds H above on the tail and is strictly below 9/50 there (the difference has numerator 2t³−27t²+150t−150 after multiplication by 150 t²(t−1)). At beta_star the symbol's maximum is attained below 2 pi: its value at pi exceeds 8/15, but the tail is at most 1309/2700 and the zero-frequency limit is 1/3. The attained threshold minimum is above 2 pi. Fixing the resulting maximizing and minimizing frequencies u<t, their ratio strictly decreases with beta, excluding every smaller beta. Every larger beta raises the value at u while the infimum cannot exceed 1/3. For beta=1/6 the lower tail estimate reduces to t³−10t²+60t−60≥0 for t≥6; the upper estimate uses the alternating Taylor bound through t^6 for sinc up to 19/5 and the decreasing envelope (1+1/t)(1+6/t²) thereafter. This gives p in [3/10,3/5]. At beta=1/2 the sine Taylor upper bound through degree 13 gives p(4)>4/3. All needed Taylor remainders have the asserted signs by decrease of the terms in the withheld tails over the stated ranges. Independent rational checks and local stationary-point diagnostics (python /workspace/review_checks.py, check 4) reproduce about 0.1747779923813 and 1.700200564562; these diagnostics do not certify global maximizing frequencies, nor are they needed for the theorem.

value.rationale: The mass coefficient is prescribed by a substantive existing construction, so optimizing it for the canonical top-hat symbol is not an arbitrary parameter search. Separation of the active frequencies turns two pointwise comparisons into a unique robust optimum, and the certified greater-than-two improvement is material for the ideal spectral model. It is a useful benchmark, not a PCG iteration or finite-element tuning guarantee.
